# ghost_codeowners_errors (Data Source)

Checks the CODEOWNERS file of a Ghost repository at a branch, tag or commit, and lists every error in it: bad syntax, and owners that don't exist or lack write access to the repository. Ghost ignores the lines with errors when it assigns code owners, so a `check` block or a `postcondition` on `length(errors) == 0` catches a CODEOWNERS file that names a team before `ghost_team_repository` grants it write access.

Ghost uses the first file it finds of `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS` and `docs/CODEOWNERS`, and checks only that one. The name is case-sensitive.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The errors in the CODEOWNERS file on the default branch.
data "ghost_codeowners_errors" "app" {
  repository = "my-org/my-repo"
}

# A branch, tag or commit SHA instead.
data "ghost_codeowners_errors" "release" {
  repository = "my-org/my-repo"
  ref        = "release/1.x"
}

# Fail the plan when the CODEOWNERS file names an owner Ghost ignores, e.g. a
# team that hasn't been given write access yet.
check "codeowners" {
  assert {
    condition = length(data.ghost_codeowners_errors.app.errors) == 0
    error_message = join("\n", [
      for e in data.ghost_codeowners_errors.app.errors : "${e.path}:${e.line}:${e.column}: ${e.message}"
    ])
  }
}

output "codeowners_file" {
  value = data.ghost_codeowners_errors.app.path
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repository` (String) The repository's full name, `owner/slug`, e.g. `ghost_repository.example.full_name`.

### Optional

- `ref` (String) The branch, tag or commit SHA (full or short) to read the CODEOWNERS file from. Defaults to the default branch. Names are case-sensitive, and a full ref is accepted only for branches (`refs/heads/…`), so name a tag without `refs/tags/`.

### Read-Only

- `errors` (Attributes List) The errors in the file, in line order. Empty when the file is valid or there is no file. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--errors))
- `id` (String) The repository's current full name, `owner/slug`. It differs from `repository` when that names a repository that has since been renamed.
- `path` (String) The CODEOWNERS file in effect: `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS` or `docs/CODEOWNERS`. Null when `ref` has none (including an empty repository) or the file is over 3 MB.
- `repository_id` (Number) The numeric ID of `repository`.

<a id="nestedatt--errors"></a>
### Nested Schema for `errors`

Read-Only:

- `column` (Number) The 1-based column where the error starts, counted in characters: `1` for a bad pattern, the owner's column for a bad owner.
- `kind` (String) What is wrong: `Invalid pattern`, `Invalid owner` (not `@user`, `@org/team` or an email address), `Unknown owner`, `Owner without write access`, `Unknown team` or `Team without write access`. A pending collaborator invitation doesn't give write access yet, and a team is unknown on a repository owned by a user.
- `line` (Number) The 1-based line number.
- `message` (String) A readable description, e.g. `Unknown owner on line 3: make sure @alice exists and has write access to the repository`.
- `path` (String) The file the error is in, the same as the top-level `path`.
- `source` (String) The whole line as written.
- `suggestion` (String) A suggested fix, when Ghost has one. Usually null.
